title: Coded Pixels, Split Speeds, Grown Type, Faces & One-Gesture Menus
description: Pixel FX with no sprites, columns at their own scroll speed, type grown as a plant, faces that look back, and a menu you never tap twice.

drops.title: Effects That Are Only Code
drops.description: Four pixel-art effects computed per pixel into an ImageData — no sprite sheet, no shader, no asset of any kind.
drops.concept: pixelfx ships 244 effects as JavaScript rather than art: each one writes bytes into a colour buffer with a separate light buffer stacked on top, and all randomness comes from a seed so a given frame is reproducible. Two kinds coexist — pure effects that are a function of time and loop seamlessly, and simulated ones that step particles. This rebuild shows one of each at 48x48, upscaled with image-rendering: pixelated.
drops.source: patch-gg/pixelfx — 244 pixel art effects, every one a small piece of code

interaction.mouse: Drag the resolution, speed and light-buffer sliders to retune all four effects at once
interaction.click: Switch palette between Ember, Frost and Toxic
interaction.touch: Effects run full-width on phones; the parameter panel hides below 760px

drops.title: Columns at Different Speeds
drops.description: Three columns, one scrollbar, three rates — and not a single scroll listener in the page.
drops.concept: Nothing scrolls independently. The page scrolls once, and each column wears a translateY whose progress is driven by animation-timeline: scroll(root block), while every tile zooms out on its own view(block) timeline as it crosses the viewport. The illusion of separate scroll speeds is just two scroll-driven animations with different ranges.

interaction.mouse: Scroll the page and watch the columns separate; tune drift, zoom and lift live
interaction.click: The panel reports whether native scroll timelines or the JS fallback is driving
interaction.touch: Two columns on phones, same scroll-driven effect

drops.title: Type That Grows
drops.description: The word is rasterised into an alpha mask, then vines climb inside it — they can only grow into the letterform.
drops.concept: Typerfy grows vines, leaves and blooms out of letterforms on a plain Canvas 2D. The trick that makes it read as typography is containment: each vine tests its next step against the glyph mask and, when the step would leave the shape, sweeps outward for a direction that stays inside. Leaves and blooms are the only things allowed to spill past the edge.

interaction.mouse: Drag vines, speed, bloom density and wind; the plant regrows from the new settings
interaction.click: Tap the canvas to replant; pick Rose Garden, Sakura or Coral Abyss
interaction.touch: Type a new word in the pill field and the mask rebuilds at phone width

drops.title: Give the App a Face
drops.description: Five SVG mascots across six states — CSS does the animation, JavaScript only aims the pupils and blinks.
drops.concept: wobnimo gives an app a mascot whose state can be bound straight to what the app is doing: idle, listening, thinking, speaking, celebrating, sleeping. The useful idea is the split — state is a data attribute that selects a CSS animation, so the whole personality lives in the stylesheet and the script only handles what CSS cannot know, which is where your pointer is.
drops.source: Pouryaak/wobnimo — ten living 3D mascots on one tiny web animation engine

interaction.mouse: Move the pointer and all ten pupils follow; tune follow strength, wobble speed and blink rate
interaction.click: Click a mascot to cycle its own state, or use the buttons to set the whole cast
interaction.touch: Tap a mascot to cycle it; keyboard users get Enter and Space on each face

drops.title: Press, Slide, Release
drops.description: A menu that opens around your finger and commits on release — one gesture from start to finish.
drops.concept: Detent's Popup replaces press-then-tap with a single continuous gesture: the options arrive centred on the pointer, already within reach, and each one catches with a detent as you sweep past so you can aim without looking. This rebuild adds the angular stickiness explicitly, flips the arc away from screen edges, and keeps a full keyboard path.
drops.source: ds-spec/detent-ui — Popup, a menu that opens around your finger

interaction.mouse: Press and hold a card, slide toward an option, release to commit
interaction.click: Tune radius, arc spread, detent strength and dead zone from the panel
interaction.touch: Built for thumbs — press-slide-release with a haptic tick on each detent
